parsed.reasoning: Both versions keep the same core content. A moves the staggered rollout to the front, which motivates the choice of controls, and keeps the TWFE description tight. It does define never-treated and not-yet-treated stores, which this audience already knows, but that costs only one sentence. B explains why TWFE is biased under staggered timing and how Callaway and Sant'Anna works. Quantitative marketing researchers know both, so this reads as textbook exposition and makes the passage much longer. B does connect its ideas well through causal links ('To avoid this'), so it wins on flow. B also has a misplaced relative clause: 'alongside the two-way fixed effects estimate, which addresses heterogeneity' attaches the clause to the TWFE estimate rather than the Callaway and Sant'Anna estimator, which is a precision error. Overall, A reads better for this venue.
